40.title: Guard null session tokens
40.body: The guard fails closed when a mobile client wakes without a token, which is what turned refreshSession into a 500. Fixes #12. Refines the approach from discussion #3.
40.author: mina

44.title: Revert the expired reason string
44.body: Restores the exact reason string missing-token. The status page matcher compares that string and dropped alerts when it changed. Fixes #15.
44.author: jonas

51.title: Cover expired tokens without changing the reason
51.body: Adds token.expired and an empty-value check while keeping the reason string missing-token, so the dashboard contract stays intact. Fixes #18.
51.author: mina

12.title: Session refresh crashes when the mobile client wakes with a null token
12.body: After the background-resume rollout, Android clients called refreshSession(null) and the API 500'd on token.value. The guard needs to fail closed.
12.author: lina

15.title: Dashboard alert matcher broke on reason missing-or-expired
15.body: The status page matcher keys on the exact string missing-token. Changing the guard's reason dropped production alerts for 40 minutes.
15.author: lina

18.title: Expired tokens still take the refresh path
18.body: Reverting the reason string was right, but expired tokens are refreshable again. Express expiry as a boolean and keep the reason string stable.
18.author: mina

3.title: Where should the null-token guard live?
3.body: The gateway could drop null tokens, but every service imports the client library. Put the guard in refreshSession so call sites cannot forget it.
3.author: ada

comments.author: sam
comments.body: Agree on the library, and keep the reason string stable. The dashboard matcher is an exact compare.

40.author: ada
40.body: Null is the crash we saw, but expiry is the same failure mode. Can the guard treat expired tokens as not refreshable without inventing a new reason string?

51.author: jonas
51.body: Checked the dashboard matcher: it still keys on missing-token. This shape is safe to ship.

40.author: ada
40.body: The fail-closed behavior is what we want. I left a note on the line about expired tokens.

12.author: lina
12.body: Saw this in production after the mobile resume rollout: refreshSession was invoked with null and threw on token.value.

15.author: lina
15.body: Alerts flatlined for 40 minutes. Please revert the reason string rather than teaching the matcher a second value.

18.author: mina
18.body: Boolean expiry keeps the matcher intact and still rejects stale tokens.
